title: Empirical Evaluation of a Generate–Validate–Repair Loop for Intent→Network Configuration Using a Deterministic Reachability Validator
abstract: We measure the marginal effect of inserting a deterministic reachability validator plus at most one automated repair (a generate–validate–repair, GVR, loop) around a single LLM (declared gpt-5-mini) for synthesising device configurations from natural-language NetOps intents. In a fully preregistered paired design (cns-m2026-01) with 300 intents (600 episodes; shared-initial semantics) the baseline generator produced execution-validated correct configurations in 299/300 tasks (99.667%). The guarded pipeline (deterministic validator ± one repair) achieved 300/300 (100.0%). Paired difference = 0.00333; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01] (10k resamples, seed=1729). Provider-call accounting shows 301 total model calls: 300 shared-initial generator calls plus a single guarded repair call. The preregistered target effect (10 percentage points) is not supported because the baseline generator was near ceiling on this task set. All model-call traces, per-episode validator traces, scoring JSON, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA‑256 hashes to enable reproducibility (Disclosure).

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are being proposed to translate operator intent into low-level device configuration (intent→configuration). For operational adoption, two properties are essential: (1) the generated configuration must satisfy the stated intent and (2) it must not introduce unintended reachability or safety regressions. Architectures that interpose a deterministic "validator" between a proposer and execution, optionally coupled with automated repair, are widely advocated; they implement a closed-loop GVR pattern that aims to catch and correct proposer mistakes before execution. This paper reports a preregistered, artifact-backed, paired experiment (cns-m2026-01) that quantifies the marginal benefit of inserting a single deterministic reachability validator plus at most one automated repair around a single LLM generator (declared gpt-5-mini). The study used shared-initial semantics: a single generator output per intent was evaluated both with and without the validator/repair stage to isolate the gate’s marginal effect on identical proposals. The work emphasizes reproducibility: every model call, provider trace, validator trace, per-episode scoring JSON, and the full analysis log are archived with SHA‑256 hashes.
sections.related_work: Prior work examines LLM-assisted network configuration, verifier-assisted pipelines, and generate–validate–repair architectures for code and configuration (selected leads include NetConfEval/intent→config evaluations and recent verifier-proposer architectures). Discussions on closed-loop verifier gates and contract-enforced architectures are widespread in the agentic-LLM literature; our contribution is a tightly preregistered, paired measurement with complete execution provenance. For background and closest prior-art see the cited records (cited_record_ids).
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: The experiment was preregistered as cns-m2026-01 (preregistration SHA‑256 = 0726a6c02c1ed6fc379927f4bb0696330f0b00484f15caee5cf4ebc072316bf7). Unit = intent (paired baseline vs guarded). N=300 intents were deterministically selected by the preregistered generator and contamination filters; the executed task manifest is archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; SHA‑256 = 91564bb69ac692e2fbd6321708863d13938309b5433ef1b211541ba5426df990). Model and calls: declared model = gpt-5-mini; configuration file execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Shared-initial semantics: for each intent a single generator call produced the candidate proposal used by both conditions. Guarded pipeline: a deterministic reachability validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5, version 5.0) checked the proposal against an emulator snapshot; if the validator rejected, at most one automated repair call was permitted (repair budget preregistered). Validator semantics (explicit): the validator executes a deterministic closed-world emulation of device state, parses the proposed commands, and checks (a) syntactic parsability, (b) that the command sequence reaches the declared final-state constraints, and (c) absence of unintended reachability or policy changes outside the allowed touched fields. “Unintended reachability change” is operationalised as any emulator-observed change to interfaces or routes not listed in the task’s allowed_touched_fields or required_sequence; validator decisions and the exact per-episode checks are recorded in per-episode validator traces (execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/). Transformation and validator artifacts: the implementation identifiers and image traces are listed in execution/transformation_manifest.json (SHA‑256 = b6ba6a75fa59f12f6b67e16aa5702f0fb95ba94cdb8d9b7e4d9b530c1ea76eb1). Analysis plan: confirmatory paired test (exact McNemar two-sided); paired difference plus 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729) as preregistered. Full execution manifest and provider-call logs are archived (execution/execution_manifest.json).
sections.results: Accounting and raw outcomes: completed_episode_count = 600 (300 pairs); model_calls_used = 301 (shared_initial_generation = 300; repair calls = 1) as recorded in the execution manifest. The single repair call corresponds to episode task-000117 (archived repair trace execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json; SHA‑256 = 4deb410d5736ab332cd5caaf00b16051e5b0aef2276255c0770098f63cb523ba). Primary paired outcome (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA‑256 = 3421adb52d5791a979397368165fc2062e6b9a4a771ce49c0bcac80b02215d55): n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Baseline success = 299/300 = 0.996667; guarded success = 300/300 = 1.0. Paired difference = 0.0033333333333332993. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the paired difference = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Per-episode exemplar artifacts: representative per-episode scoring JSON and response files are archived under execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/ (examples and SHA‑256 values are cited in Disclosure and in Example artifacts above). Missingness and deviations: failed_episode_count = 0; no post-preregistration changes to the analysis method; deterministic_reconciliation.json confirms internal accounting (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json; SHA‑256 = f6da505032ab388ceccda8e85084b53b8cada91a7ccc0dc65601385505f00ea6).
sections.discussion: Interpretation: the guarded validator+one-repair loop corrected a single isolated proposer error (the sole discordant pair) but produced only a +0.33 percentage-point aggregate change because the baseline generator performed near ceiling on the chosen deterministic task set. Operational implication: a single-step deterministic validator with a one-call repair budget can fix isolated generator errors (artifact-backed example: task-000117), but measurable aggregate benefit requires either (a) a lower-baseline-accuracy task distribution (real-world noisy/human-authored intents), (b) larger repair budgets (iterative repair), or (c) tougher validators capturing richer failure classes. Clarifications requested in review: validator semantics are explicitly summarised in Methods (above) and the transformation_manifest and per-episode validator traces contain the exact rule set and emulator snapshot identifiers (execution/transformation_manifest.json; SHA‑256 cited). Provider-call accounting: model_calls_used = 301 equals 300 shared-initial generator calls plus the single guarded repair call; the execution manifest’s provider_call_audit field records stage counts (shared_initial_generation=300, repair=1). The provider_call_audit/condition_counts fields ("shared":300, "guarded":1) are stage-level counts (shared-initial vs repair) rather than per-condition model-call totals; deterministic_reconciliation.json reconciles these counts and is authoritative. H2 (that residual failures after GVR would mainly reflect specification ambiguity) is preregistered but unassessable here because there were zero residual guarded failures; this null result is reported explicitly. Threats to validity: internal—shared-initial isolates gate effect but restricts pipeline variants evaluated; construct—the validator approximates safety as absence of emulator-observed unintended reachability change (closed-world proxy); external—the task bank was deterministic and emulator-based so external generalisability is limited; conclusion validity—ceiling effect reduces power to detect pre-specified large effects. All per-episode artifacts and hashes are archived to permit independent inspection and alternative analyses.
sections.conclusion: In this preregistered paired experiment (N=300) the addition of a deterministic reachability validator plus at most one automated repair corrected a single baseline error (299→300 successes). The preregistered target improvement (10 percentage points) is not supported because the baseline generator’s accuracy on this task set was near ceiling. The run demonstrates that verifier-assisted repairs can fix isolated mistakes and that rigorous artifact archiving enables reproducible failure analysis; however, measurable operational gains from a singlevalidator/one-repair policy will be more apparent on harder intent distributions or with expanded repair budgets. We publish the full execution and analysis artifact bundle (paths and SHA‑256s cited in Disclosure) to enable reproducible extensions (multi-iteration repair, adversarial intents, multi-model comparisons).

disclosure_statement:
Disclosure Statement — archived provenance and runtime facts

Initial master prompt immutable reference (archived): provenance/master_prompt.txt — SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba.
Preregistration: cns-m2026-01 (preregistration SHA‑256 = 0726a6c02c1ed6fc379927f4bb0696330f0b00484f15caee5cf4ebc072316bf7). This preregistration (frozen before execution) specified shared-initial semantics, inclusion/exclusion rules, contamination checks, stopping rules, paired analysis (exact McNemar two‑sided), bootstrap CI settings (10,000 resamples, seed=1729), and the repair budget (<=1 repair call).
Declared LLM and configuration: gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version). Model configuration archived at execution/model_configuration.json — SHA‑256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820.
Execution harness and artifacts (authoritative): execution/execution_manifest.json (the full manifest and hash index) and execution/transformation_manifest.json (validator/emulator identifiers). Key artifact hashes and paths cited in the manuscript: execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 91564bb69ac692e2fbd6321708863d13938309b5433ef1b211541ba5426df990), execution/transformation_manifest.json (SHA‑256 = b6ba6a75fa59f12f6b67e16aa5702f0fb95ba94cdb8d9b7e4d9b530c1ea76eb1), execution/execution_manifest.json (full trace manifest; contained within the supplied evidence bundle). The deterministic validator identifier and version are deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (version 5.0); the validator’s operational checks and emulator snapshot identifiers are enumerated in execution/transformation_manifest.json and per-episode validator traces (examples in execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/).
Provider-call accounting and cache: model_calls_used = 301 (execution manifest). This equals 300 shared-initial generator calls plus 1 observed guarded repair call; the repair trace is archived at execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json (SHA‑256 = 4deb410d5736ab332cd5caaf00b16051e5b0aef2276255c0770098f63cb523ba). Per-call provider traces and cached call artifacts are archived under execution/provider_calls/ and execution/call_cache/ (representative call-cache entry execution/call_cache/017065ac823abfb3ca9bc5eeca18c74dcd5758e0ff423848de8e42692449fed7.json; SHA‑256 = a632f9e9bbd3fff218e8cce95147832cbd707273573f31e1a21858cc42fbcff9). The execution manifest’s provider_call_audit stage-level entries (e.g., condition_counts) reflect stage counts (shared_initial vs repair) rather than per-condition model-call totals; deterministic_reconciliation.json reconciles all counts and is authoritative (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json; SHA‑256 = f6da505032ab388ceccda8e85084b53b8cada91a7ccc0dc65601385505f00ea6).
Analysis outputs and hashes: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 3421adb52d5791a979397368165fc2062e6b9a4a771ce49c0bcac80b02215d55) and analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA‑256 = 55eacb88c64f29dc9c5ce1ca7079eca9b4a94b5d3a2970dae019a81a1decf73b) are archived and correspond to the primary confirmatory counts reported in the paper.
Human role and autonomy boundary: the Research Director selected the broad topic family and permitted pre-lock infrastructure development. After the autonomy lock the system autonomously conducted literature review, gap selection, preregistration, experiment execution, artifact archiving, analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer review, and revisions. No human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. Technical retries were allowed per the preregistered policy (up to two automated retries for transient failures); failed_episode_count = 0 in the final manifest and all retries (if any) are logged in execution/execution_log.jsonl.
Limitations of disclosure: the transformation_manifest lists validator implementation and image identifiers with recorded hashes; consumers of the artifact bundle should consult that manifest to reconstruct the validator/emulator environment. No external URLs are invented here; all referenced artifact paths and SHA‑256 values point to files included in the supplied evidence bundle.
limitations: Ceiling effect: baseline success = 299/300 limits the ability to detect the preregistered 10 percentage-point improvement.
Task scope: deterministic, emulator-based intent set; external validity to noisy or adversarial real-world intents is limited.
Model scope: single declared model (gpt-5-mini); results do not imply cross-model generality.
Validator construct: safety operationalised as absence of unintended reachability changes in a closed-world emulator snapshot; real-world risk surfaces may be broader.
Repair budget: only one automated repair attempt allowed; multi-iteration repair strategies were not evaluated in this confirmatory run.
